paragraphs: Edward M. Knabusch and Edwin J. Shoemaker started Floral City Furniture in 1927, and in 1928 the newly formed company introduced its first recliner. In 1941, we were incorporated in the state of Michigan as La-Z-Boy Chair Company, and in 1996 we changed our name to La-Z-Boy Incorporated. Today, our La-Z-Boy brand is one of the most recognized brands in the furniture industry.

We are the leading global producer of reclining chairs and one of the largest manufacturers/distributors of residential furniture in the United States. The La-Z-Boy Stores retail network is the second largest retailer of single-branded furniture in the United States. We manufacture, market, import, export, distribute and retail upholstery furniture products under the La-Z-Boy®, England, and Joybird® tradenames. In addition, we import, distribute and retail accessories and casegoods (wood) furniture products under the Hammary® and Joybird® tradenames. During fiscal 2026, we also imported, distributed, and retailed accessories and casegoods (wood) furniture products under the Kincaid® and American Drew® tradenames, and following the completion of the sale of certain assets of the Kincaid® and American Drew® wholesale businesses on May 29, 2026, we continue to retail such products. Refer to Note 4, Assets Held for Sale and Note 21, Subsequent Events, to our consolidated financial statements for further information.
As of April 25, 2026, our supply chain operations included the following:
•Four major manufacturing locations and 9 distribution centers in the United States and three facilities in Mexico to support our speed-to-market and customization strategy
•A logistics company that distributes a portion of our products in the United States
•A wholesale sales office that is responsible for distribution of our product in the United Kingdom and Ireland

•A global trading company in Hong Kong that helps us manage our Asian supply chain by establishing and maintaining relationships with our Asian suppliers, as well as identifying efficiencies and savings opportunities
During fiscal 2026 we also operated an upholstery manufacturing business in the United Kingdom and as of the end of fiscal 2026, production and operations in this business have ceased.

We also participate in two consolidated joint ventures in Thailand that support our international businesses: one that operates a manufacturing facility and another that operates a wholesale sales office. Additionally, we have contracts with several suppliers in Asia to produce products that support our pure import model for Hammary®casegoods and as of May 29, 2006, a supply arrangement with the acquirer of the Kincaid®and American Drew® wholesale businesses to support our continued retail of Kincaid® and American Drew®casegoods.

We sell our products through multiple channels: directly to consumers through retail stores that we own and operate; to furniture retailers or distributors in the United States, Canada, and approximately 45 other countries, including the United Kingdom, China, Australia, and New Zealand; and through our websites, www.la-z-boy.com and www.joybird.com.

•The centerpiece of our retail distribution strategy is our network of 378 La-Z-Boy Stores, over 500 La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio® locations, and nearly 900 La-Z-Boy branded space locations, each dedicated to marketing our La-Z-Boy branded products.

◦La-Z-Boy Stores help consumers furnish their homes by combining the style, comfort, and quality of La-Z-Boy furniture with our available design services. We own 230 of the La-Z-Boy Stores, while the remainder are independently-owned and operated.

◦La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio® locations are defined spaces within larger independent retailers that are dedicated to displaying and selling La-Z-Boy branded products, while La-Z-Boy branded space locations display a curated selection of La-Z-Boy branded products within larger independent dealers. All La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio® locations and La-Z-Boy branded space locations are independently-owned and operated.

◦In total, we have approximately 8 million square feet of proprietary floor space dedicated to selling La-Z-Boy branded products in North America within our La-Z-Boy Stores and La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio® locations.

paragraphs: Our business is subject to a variety of risks. Any of the following risks could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, liquidity, or future prospects. The risks discussed below should be carefully considered, together with the other information provided in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including in Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, Item 1C. Cybersecurity, and our financial statements, including the related notes. These risk factors do not identify all risks that we face. There may be additional risks

that are presently unknown to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial that could affect us. Investors should carefully consider all risks, including those disclosed, before making an investment decision.

Declines in certain economic and market conditions that impact consumer confidence and consumer spending, or cause further disruption in our business, could negatively impact our sales, results of operations and liquidity.

The furniture industry and our business are particularly sensitive to cyclical variations in the general economy and to uncertainty regarding future economic conditions because our principal products are consumer goods that may be considered postponable discretionary purchases. Economic downturns and prolonged negative economic conditions have affected, and could continue to affect, general consumer spending, resulting in a decrease in the overall demand for such discretionary items, including residential furniture and furnishings. Factors influencing consumer spending include, among others, general economic conditions, consumer disposable income, recession and fears of recession, United States government default or shutdown or the risk of such default or shutdown, inflation, unemployment, war and fears of war, changes in global trade policies, availability of consumer credit, consumer debt levels, consumer confidence, conditions in the housing market, fuel prices, interest rates, sales tax rates, civil disturbances and terrorist activities, natural disasters, adverse weather, and health epidemics or pandemics. We are unable to identify and predict to what extent such factors may further impact consumer spending on our products in the short and long term.

The residential furniture industry is highly competitive and fragmented. We currently compete with many other manufacturers and retailers, including online retailers. Some of these competitors offer widely advertised products or are large retail furniture dealers offering their own store-branded products. Competition in the residential furniture industry is based on, among other factors, quality, style of products, perceived value, price, promotional activities, customer service and experience, omni-channel presence, and advertising. Changes in pricing and promotional activities of competitors may adversely affect our performance. In addition, due to the large number of competitors and their wide range of product offerings, we may not be able to effectively differentiate for consumers our products (in comfort, styling, finish, and other aspects of construction) from those of our competitors. The highly competitive nature of the industry means we are constantly subject to the risk of losing market share, which would likely decrease our future sales, earnings, and liquidity.

A majority of our sales are to distribution channels that rely on physical stores to merchandise and sell our products and a significant shift in consumer preference toward purchasing products online could have a material adverse effect on our sales and operating margin. Over the past several years, the furniture industry in general has experienced a shift to more online purchasing. We are attempting to meet consumers where they prefer to shop by expanding our digital and omni-channel capabilities and improving the user experience at www.la-z-boy.com to drive more traffic to both our online site and our physical stores. We also own Joybird, a leading omni-channel, direct to consumer retailer and manufacturer of upholstered furniture. Joybird sells a large portion of their product online, where there is significant competition for customer attention among online and direct-to-consumer brands.

paragraphs: We have prepared this Management's Discussion and Analysis as an aid to understanding our financial results. It should be read in conjunction with the accompanying Consolidated Financial Statements and related Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements. It also includes management's analysis of past financial results and certain potential factors that may affect future results, potential future risks and approaches that may be used to manage those risks. Refer to "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" at the beginning of this report for a discussion of factors that may cause results to differ materially. Note that our 2026, 2025 and 2024 fiscal years all included 52 weeks.

We are the leading global producer of reclining chairs and one of the largest manufacturers/distributors of residential furniture in the United States. The La-Z-Boy Stores retail network is the second largest retailer of single-branded furniture in the United States. We manufacture, market, import, export, distribute and retail upholstery furniture products under the La-Z-Boy®, England, and Joybird® tradenames. In addition, we import, distribute and retail accessories and casegoods (wood) furniture products under the Hammary® and Joybird® tradenames. During fiscal 2026, we also imported, distributed, and retailed accessories and casegoods (wood) furniture products under the Kincaid® and American Drew® tradenames, and following the completion of the sale of certain assets of the Kincaid® and American Drew® wholesale businesses on May 29, 2026, we continue to retail such products. Refer to Note 4, Assets Held for Sale and Note 21, Subsequent Events, to our consolidated financial statements for further information.
For additional information about our business, refer to Part I, Item 1, Business of this report.

As La-Z-Boy approaches its centennial anniversary in 2027, we remain focused on executing our Century Vision strategy to grow sales and market share through growth of our consumer brands, La-Z-Boy and Joybird, and sustainably grow our operating margin well beyond this milestone year. Building on a century of innovation, comfort, craftsmanship, and consumer

trust, we are working to leverage our iconic brand to expand market reach and strengthen our engagement with consumers, dealers and partners. Through continued investment in brand evolution, retail expansion, digital transformation, innovation, and consumer insights, we aim to deliver the transformational power of comfort to future generations with a consumer-first approach while honoring our almost 100 year heritage that has made La-Z-Boy one of America's most recognized and enduring brands. Our Century Vision strategy continues to have significant runway and we are executing through the following initiatives:

•Leveraging our connection to comfort and reinvigorating our brand with a consumer focus, expanded omni-channel presence, and digital transformation. Our strategic initiatives to leverage and reinvigorate our iconic La-Z-Boy brand center on a renewed focus on leveraging the compelling La-Z-Boy comfort message, accelerating our omni-channel offering, and identifying additional consumer-base growth opportunities. We leverage our consumer insights to develop and deliver meaningful product innovation, particularly in the motion and reclining categories. We also utilize consumer insights to optimize our messaging and marketing campaigns to increase recognition and consideration of La-Z-Boy among both existing and prospective customers. Our Long Live the Lazy campaign, launched in 2024, continues to resonate through its compelling, consumer-inspired message. In 2025, we successfully launched a refreshed brand identity - the first significant evolution of the La-Z-Boy brand in more than two decades - designed to modernize the brand, enhance differentiation, and strengthen relevance with a broader consumer audience across retail and digital footprints. Further, our goal is to connect with consumers along their purchase journey through multiple means, whether online or in person. We are driving change throughout our digital platforms to improve the user experience, with a specific focus on the ease with which customers browse through our broad product assortment, customize products to their liking, find stores to make a purchase, or purchase at www.la-z-boy.com. We believe that our digital transformation will improve traffic both online and in our retail locations.

•Growing our La-Z-Boy retail business. We expect to grow our Retail segment through organic same-store sales growth and by increasing company-owned stores through the opening of new stores and acquisitions. Opportunistically acquiring existing La-Z-Boy Stores and opening new La-Z-Boy Stores where we see opportunity for growth or further market penetration continues to be a priority. Over the last five years, as a result of opening new company-owned stores and acquiring independent La-Z-Boy Stores, we have increased our ownership percentage in this store network from 45% to 61%. With 378 stores currently in the La-Z-Boy Store network, we believe there is opportunity to open approximately ten stores annually, with the majority being company-owned, targeting a network of 450 stores.

•Expanding the reach of our wholesale distribution channels. Consumers experience the La-Z-Boy brand in many channels including the La-Z-Boy Store network, the La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio® locations, our store-within-a-store format, and La-Z-Boy branded space locations. While consumers increasingly interact with the brand digitally, our consumers also demonstrate an affinity for visiting our stores to shop, allowing us to frequently deliver the flagship La-Z-Boy Store, La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio®, or La-Z-Boy branded space experience and provide design services. In addition to our branded distribution channels, over 1,000 other dealers sell La-Z-Boy products, which include some of the best-known names in the industry, providing us the benefit of multi-channel distribution. We believe there is significant growth potential for our consumer brands through these retail channels.

•Profitably growing the Joybird brand with a digital-first consumer experience. Joybird is a leading omni-channel, direct to consumer retailer and manufacturer of upholstered furniture. We believe that Joybird is a brand with significant long-term potential and our strategic initiatives in this area focus on driving profitable growth through the opening of additional small-format stores in key markets, expanding distribution channels, driving customer acquisition and awareness through digital marketing, and continued optimization of cost structure.

•Enhancing our enterprise capabilities to support the growth of our consumer brands and enable potential acquisitions for growth. Key to successful growth is ensuring we have the capabilities to support that growth, including an agile supply chain, modern technology for consumers, employees, and analytic capabilities, and by delivering a human-centered employee experience. We continue to have initiatives focused on enhancing these capabilities with a consumer-first focus.
Our reportable operating segments include the Retail segment and the Wholesale segment.

•Retail Segment. Our Retail segment consists of one operating segment comprised of our 230 company-owned La-Z-Boy Stores. The Retail segment sells primarily upholstered furniture, in addition to some casegoods and other home furnishing accessories, to end consumers through these stores.

•Wholesale Segment. Our Wholesale segment consists primarily of four operating segments: La-Z-Boy, our largest operating segment, our England subsidiary, our casegoods operating segment that sells furniture under three brands (American Drew®, Hammary®, and Kincaid®), and our international operating segment which includes our international La-Z-Boy wholesale and manufacturing businesses. We aggregate these operating segments into one reportable segment because they are economically similar and meet the other aggregation criteria for determining reportable segments. Our Wholesale segment manufactures and imports upholstered furniture, such as recliners and motion furniture, sofas, loveseats, chairs, sectionals, modulars, ottomans and sleeper sofas and imports casegoods (wood) furniture such as bedroom sets, dining room sets, entertainment centers and occasional pieces. The Wholesale segment sells directly to La-Z-Boy Stores, operators of La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio® and branded space locations, England Custom Comfort Center locations, major dealers, and a wide cross-section of other independent retailers.

•Corporate and Other. Corporate and Other includes the shared costs for corporate functions, including human resources, information technology, finance and accounting, and legal, in addition to revenue generated through royalty agreements with companies licensed to use the La-Z-Boy® brand name on various products. We consider our corporate functions to be other business activities and have aggregated them with our other insignificant operating segments, including our global trading company in Hong Kong and Joybird, an omni-channel retailer that manufactures upholstered furniture such as sofas, loveseats, chairs, ottomans, sleeper sofas and beds, and also imports casegoods (wood) furniture such as occasional tables and other accessories. Joybird sells to the end consumer online through its website, www.joybird.com, through small-format stores in key markets, and through other distribution channels. None of the operating segments included in Corporate and Other meet the requirements of reportable segments.

paragraphs: Edward M. Knabusch 和 Edwin J. Shoemaker 於 1927 年創立 Floral City Furniture，並於 1928 年新成立的公司推出其第一款躺椅。1941 年，本公司在密歇根州註冊為 La-Z-Boy Chair Company，並於 1996 年將公司名稱更為 La-Z-Boy Incorporated。目前，本公司 La-Z-Boy 品牌為傢俱產業中最具辨識度的品牌之一。

本公司為全球躺椅的主要生產商，並為美國住宅傢俱的最大製造/經銷商之一。La-Z-Boy Stores 零售網路為美國單品牌傢俱零售第二大零售商。本公司在 La-Z-Boy®、England 及 Joybird® 商標下製造、行銷、進口、出口、經銷與零售包覆傢俱產品。此外，本公司亦在 Hammary® 及 Joybird® 商標下進口、經銷與零售配件與木製傢俱產品。在財務年度 2026 年，本公司亦在 Kincaid® 及 American Drew® 商標下進口、經銷與零售配件與木製傢俱產品，並於 2026 年 5 月 29 日完成 Kincaid® 及 American Drew® 批發業務部分資產的出售後，本公司仍持續零售這些產品。有關進一步資訊，請參閱我們合併財務報表的附註 4，Assets Held for Sale 以及附註 21，Subsequent Events。
截至 2026 年 4 月 25 日，本公司供應鏈運作包含以下內容：
•四個主要製造廠與九個配送中心位於美國，以及三個設施位於墨西哥，以支持本公司快速上市與客製化策略
•一家物流公司在美國經銷本公司部分產品
•一家批發銷售辦事處，負責本公司產品在英國與愛爾蘭的經銷
•一家位於香港的全球貿易公司，協助本公司管理亞洲供應鏈，透過建立與維護本公司亞洲供應商的關係，以及識別效率與節省成本的機會
在財務年度 2026 年，本公司亦經營一家位於英國的包覆傢俱製造業務，並於財務年度 2026 年結束時，該業務的生產與運作已停止。

我們亦參與泰國兩家合資企業，支援我們的國際業務：一家經營製造廠，另一家經營批發銷售辦事處。此外，我們與亞洲數家供應商簽有合約，用以生產支援我們純進口模式的產品，用於 Hammary® 案件傢俱，並自 2006 年 5 月 29 日起，與 Kincaid® 和 American Drew® 批發業務的買受人有供應安排，以支援我們持續銷售 Kincaid® 和 American Drew® 案件傢俱。
我們透過多種通路銷售產品：直接對消費者透過我們擁有並經營的零售商店；對美國、加拿大及約 45 個其他國家的傢俱零售商或經銷商，包括英國、中國、澳洲和紐西蘭；以及透過我們的網站，www.la-z-boy.com 和 www.joybird.com。
• 我們零售通路策略的核心是我們擁有 378 家 La-Z-Boy 商店、超過 500 家 La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio® 通路點，以及近 900 家 La-Z-Boy 品牌空間通路點，專門用以行銷我們的 La-Z-Boy 品牌產品。
◦ La-Z-Boy 商店協助消費者裝潢住宅，將 La-Z-Boy 傢俱的風格、舒適度與品質與我們的設計服務結合。我們擁有 230 家 La-Z-Boy 商店，其餘則為獨立擁有並經營。
◦ La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio® 通路點為大型獨立零售商內專門用以展示與銷售 La-Z-Boy 品牌產品的空間，而 La-Z-Boy 品牌空間通路點則在大型獨立經銷商內展示精心挑選的 La-Z-Boy 品牌產品。所有 La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio® 通路點與 La-Z-Boy 品牌空間通路點皆為獨立擁有並經營。
◦ 總計，我們在北美地區於 La-Z-Boy 商店與 La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio® 通路點內，專門用以銷售 La-Z-Boy 品牌產品的自有樓地板空間約為 8 百萬平方英呎。

paragraphs: 我們已準備此管理層討論與分析，作為瞭解我們財務結果的輔助工具。應與隨附的合併財務報表及相關合併財務報表附註一併閱讀。此段亦包含管理層對過去財務結果的分析，以及可能影響未來結果的某些潛在因素、潛在未來風險，以及可能用來管理這些風險的方法。請參閱本報告開頭的「警示未來聲明」，以瞭解可能導致結果有重大差異的因素。請注意，我們 2026、2025 及 2024 財年均包含 52 週。

我們是全球領先的躺椅製造商，也是美國住宅傢俱最大的製造商/經銷商之一。La-Z-Boy 零售網路是美國第二大單品牌傢俱零售商。我們在 La-Z-Boy®、England 及 Joybird® 商標下製造、行銷、進口、出口、經銷與零售包覆傢俱產品。此外，我們也在 Hammary® 及 Joybird® 商標下進口、經銷與零售配件與木製傢俱產品。在 2026 財年，我們也在 Kincaid® 及 American Drew® 商標下進口、經銷與零售配件與木製傢俱產品，並在 2026 年 5 月 29 日完成 Kincaid® 及 American Drew® 批發業務部分資產的出售後，我們仍持續零售這些產品。請參閱我們合併財務報表的附註 4，資產待售，以及附註 21，後續事件，以取得更多資訊。
如需更多關於我們業務的資訊，請參閱本報告的 Part I，Item 1，業務。
隨著 La-Z-Boy 即將在 2027 年邁入百年紀念，我們仍專注於執行我們的世紀願景策略，透過我們的消費者品牌 La-Z-Boy 及 Joybird 的成長，來增加銷售與市佔率，並可持續地將營運毛利成長至超越這個里程碑年份。建立在一個世紀的創新、舒適、工藝與消費者
我們致力於善用我們的經典品牌，擴大市場觸角並強化與消費者、經銷商及夥伴的互動。透過持續投資於品牌演進、零售擴張、數位轉型、創新及消費者洞察，我們旨在以消費者為先的策略，將舒適的變革力量傳遞給未來世代，同時尊重我們近百年來的傳統，使La-Z-Boy成為美國最知名且歷久彌新的品牌之一。我們的世紀願景策略仍有相當大的發展空間，我們正透過以下計畫執行：

•善用我們與舒適的連結，並以消費者為焦點，擴大全通路存在與數位轉型。我們的戰略計畫旨在善用並重振我們的經典La-Z-Boy品牌，重點在於重新聚焦於強大的La-Z-Boy舒適訊息，加速我們的全通路方案，並尋找更多的消費者基礎成長機會。我們利用消費者洞察來開發並提供有意義的產品創新，特別是在動態與傾斜類別。我們也運用消費者洞察來優化我們的訊息與行銷活動，以提高La-Z-Boy在現有及潛在客戶中的認知與考慮度。我們於2024年啟動的Long Live the Lazy活動，其強烈的消費者啟發訊息持續引起共鳴。在2025年，我們成功推出一個更新的品牌形象－這是超過二十年來首次對La-Z-Boy品牌進行的重大演進，旨在現代化品牌、增強差異化並強化與更廣泛消費者羣體的相關性，無論是在零售與數位通路上。此外，我們的目標是透過多種方式與消費者在其購買新旅程中建立連結，無論是線上或線下。我們正在推動數位平台的變革，以改善用戶體驗，特別著重於客戶瀏覽我們廣泛產品組合的便捷性、根據個人喜好客製化產品、尋找商店進行購買，或透過www.la-z-boy.com進行購買。我們相信，我們的數位轉型將會提高我們線上與零售據點的流量。

•擴大我們的La-Z-Boy零售業務。我們預期透過內生性同店銷售成長與增加公司自有商店數量（透過開設新店與收購）來成長零售部門。有機地收購現有La-Z-Boy商店與開設新La-Z-Boy商店，於我們認為有成長或進一步市場滲透機會的地區持續為優先事項。在過去五年，由於開設新公司自有商店與收購獨立La-Z-Boy商店，我們已將在該商店網路中的持股比例從45%提高至61%。目前La-Z-Boy商店網路共有378間商店，我們認為每年有機會開設約十間商店，其中大多數為公司自有商店，目標建立450間商店的網路。

•擴展我們的經銷通路。消費者在許多通路體驗La-Z-Boy品牌，包括La-Z-Boy商店網路、La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio®門店、我們的商店內商店格式，以及La-Z-Boy品牌空間門店。雖然消費者越來越透過數位方式與品牌互動，但我們的消費者也表現出對造訪我們商店購物的偏好，使我們能經常提供旗艦La-Z-Boy商店、La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio®或La-Z-Boy品牌空間的體驗並提供設計服務。除了我們的品牌通路外，超過1,000間其他經銷商銷售La-Z-Boy產品，包括業內一些最知名的品牌，為我們帶來多通路的優勢。我們相信，透過這些零售通路，我們的消費者品牌有相當大的成長潛力。
•以數位為先的消費者體驗，成功成長 Joybird 品牌。Joybird 是一家領導的全通路、直接對消費者零售與製造 upholstered furniture 的品牌。我們認為 Joybird 是一個具備顯著長期潛力的品牌，我們在這方面的戰略性計畫聚焦於透過在關鍵市場開設更多小型店面、擴展銷售通路、透過數位行銷推動消費者取得與認知，以及持續優化成本結構，來實現獲利成長。
•強化企業能力以支持消費者品牌的成長並啟動潛在收購以實現成長。成功成長的關鍵在於確保我們擁有支持成長的能力，包括靈活的供應鏈、現代化的消費者、員工與分析能力，以及提供以人為中心的員工體驗。我們持續有計畫強化這些能力，並以消費者為先的重點進行。
我們的應報告分部包括零售分部與 Wholesale 分部。
•零售分部。我們的零售分部包含一個運營分部，由我們的 230 家公司自有 La-Z-Boy 店鋪組成。零售分部主要銷售 upholstered furniture，以及一些 casegoods 和其他居家傢俱配件，透過這些店面直接銷售給終端消費者。

•Wholesale 分部。我們的 Wholesale 分部主要由四個運營分部組成：La-Z-Boy，這是我們最大的運營分部，我們的 England 子公司，我們的 casegoods 運營分部，銷售傢俱於三個品牌（American Drew®、Hammary® 和 Kincaid®），以及我們的國際運營分部，包含我們的國際 La-Z-Boy Wholesale 與製造業務。我們將這些運營分部歸納為一個應報告分部，因為它們在經濟上相似且符合其他歸納標準以確定應報告分部。我們的 Wholesale 分部製造與進口 upholstered furniture，例如 recliners 和 motion furniture、sofas、loveseats、chairs、sectionals、modulars、ottomans 和 sleeper sofas，並進口 casegoods（木製）傢俱，例如臥室組、餐廳組、娛樂中心和偶發傢俱。Wholesale 分部直接銷售給 La-Z-Boy 店鋪、La-Z-Boy Comfort Studio® 的經營者和品牌空間位置、England Custom Comfort Center 位置、主要經銷商以及廣泛的其他獨立零售商。

•企業與其他。企業與其他包括企業功能的共同成本，包括人力資源、資訊科技、財務與會計，以及法律，以及透過 royalty 協議與使用 La-Z-Boy® 品牌名稱在各種產品上的授權公司所產生的收入。我們將企業功能視為其他商業活動，並將其與我們的其他不顯著運營分部歸納在一起，包括我們在香港的全球貿易公司以及 Joybird，這是一家全通路零售商，製造 upholstered furniture，例如 sofas、loveseats、chairs、ottomans、sleeper sofas 和 beds，並進口 casegoods（木製）傢俱，例如偶發桌子和其他配件。Joybird 透過其網站 www.joybird.com 網路銷售給終端消費者，透過關鍵市場的小型店面，以及透過其他銷售通路。企業與其他所包含的運營分部均不符合應報告分部的標準。

headings: 總體經濟與市場風險因素
因競爭而失去市場佔有率及其他財務或營運困難，將可能導致我司銷售額、獲利及流動性下降。
資訊科技系統中斷可能對我司業務及營運成果產生不利影響。
供應鏈重大中斷可能對我司業務及營運成果產生不利影響。
我司可能需要從外部取得資金，但可能無法取得所需金額或成本高於預期，因而導致我司費用及營運成果受到不利影響。
法律、稅務與監管風險因素
國內或國際監管環境的變動可能對本公司業務及營運成果產生負面影響。
本公司面臨因美國或其他外國政府調整貿易政策，包括關稅及進出口規範而產生的風險。
本公司國際業務的監管變動，包括反貪污法律及規範，可能對本公司業務及營運成果產生負面影響。
本公司可能面臨產品責任及其他聲請，或需召回一項或多項產品，此情形可能對本公司聲譽、業務、營運成果及財務狀況產生負面影響。
稅務政策的變動可能對本公司業務及營運成果產生負面影響。
本公司會做出某些假設、判斷及估計，這些會影響本公司合併財務報表中所報導的金額，若這些假設、判斷及估計不正確，可能影響本公司財務結果。
paragraphs: 本公司業務面臨多種風險。上述任何風險都可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果、流動性或未來展望造成重大且不利的影響。下列討論的風險應與本年度10-K表報表中提供的其他資訊一併審慎考量，包括管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析（Item 1C）、風險因素與我們的財務報表，包括相關附註。這些風險因素並未涵蓋本公司所面臨的所有風險。尚有其他風險，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為不重要，但可能影響本公司。
投資人應在做出投資決定前，仔細考量所有風險，包括已揭露的風險。
若某些經濟與市場條件下降，影響消費者信心與消費支出，或造成本公司業務進一步中斷，可能對我們的銷售、營運成果與流動性造成負面影響。

傢俱產業與本公司業務特別敏感於總體經濟的週期性變動，以及對未來經濟條件的不確定性，因為我們的主要產品為消費者商品，可能被視為可延後的非必要性支出。經濟衰退與持續的負面經濟條件已影響，且可能繼續影響，總體消費者支出，導致對這些非必要性商品的總體需求減少，包括住宅傢俱與裝潢用品。影響消費者支出的因素包括，但不限於總體經濟狀況、消費者可支配所得、經濟衰退與對經濟衰退的擔憂、美國政府違約或停擺或違約或停擺的風險、通貨膨脹、失業率、戰爭與對戰爭的擔憂、全球貿易政策的變動、消費者信貸的可取得性、消費者負債水平、消費者信心、住宅市場狀況、燃料價格、利率、銷售稅率、社會動亂與恐怖活動、自然災害、惡劣天氣，以及健康疫情或大流行病。我們無法識別並預測這些因素在短期與長期內可能對消費者對我們產品的支出造成多大影響。

住宅傢俱產業競爭激烈且分散。我們目前與許多其他製造商與零售商競爭，包括線上零售商。其中一些競爭對手提供廣為宣傳的產品，或為大型零售傢俱經銷商，提供自有品牌產品。住宅傢俱產業的競爭基於多種因素，包括產品品質、產品風格、被認為的價值、價格、促銷活動、客戶服務與體驗、全通路存在性與廣告。競爭對手的價格與促銷活動變動可能對我們的表現造成不利影響。此外，由於競爭對手眾多且產品種類廣泛，我們可能無法有效區分我們的產品（在舒適度、風格、表面處理及其他構造方面）與競爭對手的產品。

我們銷售的大多數產品是透過依賴實體店面販售與展示的通路進行銷售，若消費者偏好大幅轉向線上購物，可能對我們的銷售與營業毛利造成重大不利影響。在過去幾年，傢俱產業整體已出現向線上購物轉移的趨勢。我們正努力在消費者偏好的購物地點進行服務，透過擴充我們的數位與全通路能力，並改善www.la-z-boy.com網站的使用者體驗，以吸引更多流量至我們的線上商店與實體店面。我們也擁有Joybird，為一家領先的全通路、直接對消費者銷售與製造 upholstered 傢俱的零售商。Joybird 的大部分產品是透過線上銷售，線上與直接對消費者品牌之間對消費者注意力的競爭非常激烈。
